parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits sharply. Federally, a trans visitor faces documented, near-universal exposure: 2025 orders bar X/non-birth-sex passport markers, a February 2025 cable orders visa refusal where document discrepancies cast doubt on sex with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and eight foreign governments issued travel advisories over identity-document rules. Federally funded single-sex facilities are closed to trans people. But the state layer is strongly protective: public-accommodations and services coverage since 2018/2020, hate-crime enhancements, panic defence abolished, a July 2026 civil-rights win enforced, an August 2024 ruling protecting trans students, and 88% polling support. Evidenced street hostility (72 raw-count incidents) meets working recourse here, unlike much of the country.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal: Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, with fraud-based lifetime ineligibility considered; X markers barred for new issues; documented confiscations stranding trans travellers; foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; litigation pending; state driver's licences have offered M/F/X since 2020-2021 (climate signal, not visitor protection).
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal is federal and precedes any state protection attaching; a mismatch at the border cannot be cured by state equality law.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal custody records show conversion-therapy-style policies for trans inmates and abuse of trans immigration detainees; bathroom-trespass arrest documented in another unit, not here. Visitor-facing custody here not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State civil-rights statute enforced (July 2026 ruling); hate-crime enhancements; panic defence abolished 2024; no documented visitor detention in this unit.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any state arrest routes into state custody rules that are less hostile than federal custody, but federal custody applies if immigration status becomes an issue.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities — a universal exposure in federal buildings. Many units ban facility use; this unit's position on the map is not stated.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodations coverage since June 2018/Jan 2020; August 2024 highest-court ruling protecting trans students on privacy/autonomy grounds.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection governs private and state buildings; federal exclusion governs federally funded sites regardless.

care_services.exposure: State bans on minor gender-affirming care (2024, expanded Jan 2026) with provider discipline and private right of suit — bites a travelling family if a trans minor needs routine or emergency gender-related care; federal orders hostile to minor care.
care_services.protection: Conversion therapy banned since 2019; public-insurance transition coverage ban lifted 2017; emergency care for adults not documented as restricted.
care_services.interaction: A visiting trans minor with a parent can be denied care the home country provides, with no state remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders and May 2026 counterterrorism language framing 'radically pro-transgender' ideology as extremist-adjacent; an attributed claim this became the least safe unit in its region for trans citizens.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2022 poll: 88% of residents support SOGI protections; a permit-discrimination bill was vetoed; failed efforts to repeal conversion-therapy ban.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises outing probability at official contact; state public opinion and enforcement buffer street-level encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Sports ban (grades 5-12, birth-certificate requirement, stay status unresolved), care bans, parent opt-outs of gender-identity instruction, and a federal order directing criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: State highest court protected trans students (Aug 2024); anti-bullying law covers gender identity/expression; a bill permitting discrimination against trans people was vetoed.
minors_guardians.interaction: Federal threat-framing of adults facilitating minors' transition creates risk for a visiting parent accompanying a trans child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025 — second-highest raw count nationally, but no per-capita denominator, so relative rate is unknown.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented civil-rights enforcement against a assailant of a trans woman (July 2026); hate-crime penalty enhancements since Oct 2019; panic defence abolished.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence risk is real but paired with working prosecution and civil remedies in this unit, unlike tier-3 thin-recourse jurisdictions.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport litigation, executive-order challenges and care-rule injunctions unresolved; sports-ban appeal status unrecorded; practical exposure varies by date of travel.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit over passport markers; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; several federal orders blocked or enjoined; functioning state courts.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty is about which federal measures are operative, not about whether state remedies exist.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.55-B, entry carries discretionary screening and possible refusal with slow remedies, and outcomes vary. This dossier is higher because in-country life has broad, enforced accommodations coverage, hate-crime penalties and 88% public support, so post-entry severity is materially lower than the anchor's humiliating, rarely-revised border-centric picture.

Similar to 0.65-C: courts enforce remedies predictably, custody never plausible, documented official recourse works (July 2026 civil-rights ruling, August 2024 student ruling). Lower than 0.65-C because the entry/document regime is actively restrictive and federally hostile, not merely silent, and documented street incidents are frequent.

Lower than 0.75-C: that anchor has trained border officers, respectful inspection and tribunal appeals. Here the federal cable affirmatively directs refusal on sex-doubt and considers lifetime fraud findings, and federal facility exclusion applies — universal exposures absent from 0.75-C — despite stronger everyday state protections.

Higher than 0.45-D: no mandatory identity registration, hotel-nightly reporting, or durable database exposure for visitors is documented. The federal document regime bites at entry rather than continuously through daily services, and state anti-discrimination law bars most service refusals.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets two regimes in sequence. At the border and in federally funded facilities the national framework is documented and hostile: document-discrepancy refusals, possible lifetime fraud findings, X-marker elimination, exclusion from federally funded single-sex facilities, and official rhetoric that raises outing probability at every official contact. Once inside this state, the operative regime inverts: broad public-accommodations and services coverage, enforced civil-rights law with a 2026 win, hate-crime enhancements, an abolished panic defence, a court protecting trans students, and a strongly supportive electorate. The residual exposures are entry friction (which can strand or bar the traveller before state protection matters), federal-building facility exclusion, minor-care bans affecting a travelling trans child, and a high raw incident count whose per-capita rate is unknown. Working remedies and aligned state law pull this into the low-60s; the federal layer keeps it out of the 0.75 band.
